State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
Ashish Jain vs Apple India on 4 September, 2017
STATE CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION, PUNJAB,
 CHANDIGARH.

 First Appeal No.421 of 2017

 Date of institution : 07.06.2017
 Date of decision : 04.09.2017

Ashish Jain son of Shri Keemat Lal Jain, resident of H.No.3776/1,
Street No.14, New Madhopuri, Sundar Nagar, Ludhiana.
 .......Appellant-Complainant
 Versus

 1. Apple India, 19th Floor, Concorde Tower, C, UB City, 24, Vittal
 Malaya Road, Bangalore-560 001 through its Authorised
 Representative.
 2. Reliance Communication Limited, A Block, 2nd Floor, DAKC,
 Kopan Khairane, Navi Mumbai through its authorized
 representative.
 3. F-1 Info Solutions and Services Private Limited, 58-A, Model
 Gram, Near Kochar Market, Ludhiana through its authorized
 representative.
 ........Respondents-Opposite Parties

 First Appeal against the order dated
 6.4.2017 of the District Consumer
 Disputes Redressal Forum, Ludhiana.
Quorum:-
 Hon'ble Mr. Justice Paramjeet Singh Dhaliwal, President
 Mrs. Kiran Sibal, Member
Present:-
For the appellant : Shri C.K. Jha, Advocate.
For respondent No.1&3: Shri Devinder Kumar, Advocate.
 For respondent No.2 :Shri Ammish Goel, Advocate.

JUSTICE PARAMJEET SINGH DHALIWAL, PRESIDENT:
The instant appeal has been filed by the appellant/complainant

against the order dated 6.4.2017 passed by District Consumer

Disputes Redressal Forum, Ludhiana (in short, "the District Forum"),

whereby the complaint filed by him, under Section 12 of the
First Appeal No.421 of 2017 2
Consumer Protection Act, 1986
(in short, "
C.P. Act
") for issuance of

following directions to the opposite parties:-
i) to refund, replace or repair his i-phone;

 ii) to pay compensation of ₹25,000/- on account of mental

 tension, pain and agony; and

 iii) to pay ₹11,000/-, as litigation expenses,

was dismissed.
2. It would be apposite to mention that hereinafter the parties will

be referred, as have been arrayed before the District Forum.
3. Brief facts, for the disposal of the present appeal, are that the

complainant purchased an Apple i-phone 5S, 16 GB MM, Silver

Colour bearing product serial/IMEI No.358690056911296

manufactured by opposite party No.1 through opposite party No.2,

vide Invoice No.IN003036 dated 12.12.2013 by paying ₹61,856/-
under the Scheme of Reliance Truly Unlimited Plan for 24 months.

The amount was to be paid in monthly instalments at the rate of

₹2,999/-, payable in 24 Equal Monthly Instalments. In the first week

of November 2014 some problem occurred in the display of this

mobile phone and half of the display screen became black suddenly.

The complainant claimed that he had been keeping the i-phone in

good condition and had been using the same carefully and

cautiously. On 7.11.2014 the complainant deposited the said mobile

phone in question with opposite party No.3 i.e. Service Centre of

opposite party No.1. After checking, the said mobile phone was

returned to the complainant by claiming that damage had occurred,

which could not be repaired under warranty. For repair, demand of
First Appeal No.421 of 2017 3
₹21,500/- was made. Despite repeated requests, the mobile phone

has neither been repaired nor replaced nor the price of the same has

been refunded. As such, registered legal notice dated 17.11.2014

was served upon opposite parties through his counsel but no reply

thereto has been received. Alleging deficiency in service on the part

of the opposite parties, the present complaint was filed by the

complainant in the District Forum praying the aforesaid relief.
4. It needs to be noticed that earlier this complaint was allowed,

vide order dated 17.4.2015 passed by the District Forum. Against

that order, FA No.604 of 2015 was preferred by opposite party No.1.

The same was allowed and the order dated 17.4.2015 was set aside.

The case was remanded back to the District Forum for deciding the

same afresh by proceeding in accordance with the provisions of the
C.P. Act
. After receipt of the consumer complaint, separate written

statements were filed by opposite parties Nos.1 and 2 and opposite

party No.3 preferred to remain ex parte before the District Forum.

Thereafter the present impugned order has been passed.

Defence of opposite party No.1:
5. Opposite party No.1 in its reply claimed that the complaint has

been filed with mala fide intention, which is devoid of merits. The

consumers, who willfully destroy, damage or negligently handle the

product, are not eligible to claim relief under the
C.P. Act
and in case

damage to the product caused by external factors, then benefit of

warranty clauses is not available. So far as the purchase of the

mobile phone is concerned, the same was admitted. Rather it is

claimed that opposite party No.3, the Service Centre of opposite
First Appeal No.421 of 2017 4
party No.1, made diligent efforts for diagnosing the problem, when

the mobile phone was brought to it on 7.11.2014. Opposite party

No.3 after thorough technical analysis and visual mechanical

inspection found that the display of the mobile phone had turned

black and there were lines on it. Opposite Party No.1 found that all

that occurred due to pressure damage with the display. Services

were offered to be provided on payment basis because the loss

occurred due to pressure damage and claim was not covered under

the warranty clauses. The complainant alleged that it was a

manufacturing defect but actually it is own fault of the complainant

that he had caused damage by exerting high pressure on the screen.

It was admitted that the complainant had deposited the mobile phone

with opposite party No.3 on 7.11.2014 and the repair bill of the

mobile phone amounting to ₹21,500/- was also admitted. Thus the

damage to the mobile phone was not covered under the warranty

clause. A prayer for dismissal of the complaint qua it has been

made.
Defence of opposite party No.2:
6. Opposite party No.2 filed its separate reply almost on the

identical lines as has been filed by opposite party No.1. It was

pleaded that the complainant has no locus-standi to file the

complaint against opposite party No.2 under
Section 7-B
of the

Indian Telegraph Act. Opposite party No.2 has only sold the mobile

set and the defects and other liabilities are of the manufacturer.

Damage to the product had been caused due to illegal act of the
First Appeal No.421 of 2017 5
complainant. Denying all other allegations made in the complaint, a

prayer for dismissal of the complaint has been made.
7. The parties produced evidence in support of their respective

averments before the District Forum, which after going through the

same and hearing learned counsel on their behalf, dismissed the

complaint, vide impugned order. Hence, this appeal.
8. We have heard learned counsel for the parties and have

carefully gone through the records of the case.

Contentions of the Parties:
9. Learned counsel for the complainant has vehemently

contended that Ex.C-4 and Ex.R-3 is one and the same document

i.e. Service Delivery Challan. In this document reason/cause of

damage has not been mentioned. Due service was not provided by

the Service Centre. It is alleged that opposite party No.3 had

discussed the problem with him and it was specifically stated that it

was a case of pressure damage and due to pressure display screen

damaged and turned half black. It has further been contended that

since the i-phone is under the warranty period, therefore, the same

should be replaced or repaired free of cost by the opposite parties.

The District Forum committed an illegality and infirmity while

dismissing the complaint. It has been prayed that this appeal be

allowed; the impugned order passed by the District Forum be set

aside; and the complaint be allowed as prayed for.
10. On the other hand, learned counsel for opposite party No.1 has

vehemently contended that damage was on account of external

cause and the warranty is not applicable to the damage caused by
First Appeal No.421 of 2017 6
accident, abuse, misuse, fire, earthquake or other external cause.

Exerting of pressure on the mobile certainly falls in the category of

damage on account of external cause. Therefore, the complainant is

not entitled to free repair in view of putting of pressure on the mobile

phone. He prayed that there is no merit in the present appeal and

the same is liable to be dismissed.
11. Learned counsel for opposite party No.2 has vehemently

contended that opposite party No.2 is only the seller and the

warranty, if any, is to be provided by opposite party No.1-

manufacturer. Moreover, the damage to the mobile phone in

question has been caused due to external pressure put on the

mobile phone and, as such, the benefit of warranty clauses cannot

be given. The District Forum has committed no illegality or infirmity

in passing the impugned order and the same is liable to be upheld.

Consideration of Contentions:
12. We have given our thoughtful consideration to the contentions

raised by the learned counsel for the parties.
13. Against the column "Problem Reported" in Service Delivery

Challan, Ex.C-4/Ex.R-3, it has been mentioned that "DUE TO

PRESSURE DAMAGE DISPLAY DAMAGE & HALF SCREEN

BLACK". The said Delivery Challan is dated 7.11.2014 and the

mobile phone was also returned on the same day. The complainant

has admitted this fact that opposite party No.3-Service Centre had

returned the i-phone saying that it could not be repaired under

warranty and demanded ₹21,500/- for repairing the same and the

cause of defect has also been clearly mentioned as due to external
First Appeal No.421 of 2017 7
pressure put on the phone, which is not covered under the warranty.

For that reason the complainant was asked to pay the amount of

₹21,500/- for repairing the mobile phone in question. Once the

damage has been caused due to the negligence of the complainant

himself, as the pressure was exerted on the display screen, which

resulted into non-display and half of it turned black, the warranty

does not apply. For this view, there is categorical finding recorded

by the District Forum that this defect had occurred due to the

external pressure and was not a manufacturing defect or otherwise

defect. For that reason the damage caused to the mobile phone is

not covered under the warranty.
14. In view of this, we do not find any illegality or perversity in the

impugned order passed by the District Forum. There is no merit in

the present appeal and the same is hereby dismissed.
(JUSTICE PARAMJEET SINGH DHALIWAL)
 PRESIDENT

 (MRS. KIRAN SIBAL)
 MEMBER
September 04, 2017
Bansal
